Floodwater out of Whitlow Canyon led to the closure of Silver King Rd. The employee from Queen Valley Fire Department said it was the highest flow he has ever seen. A Pinal County Flood Control streamflow gauge on Queen Creek at El Camino Viejo measured peak flow around 7 feet. No damages or injuries were reported.

A truck driver went around barricades trying to cross Tonto Creek along East Greenback Valley Road, but got stuck and had to be rescued by the Arizona Public Safety Ranger helicopter. The driver was unharmed. Timing based on the 911 call received from a Gila County Sheriff Officer. No injuries were reported.
A 61 mph wind gust was measured at El Centro Naval Facility.
A 60 mph wind gust was measured at the Imperial County Airport.
A 62 mph wind gust was measured at the El Centro Naval Facility.

A couple from Rhode Island started hiking around noon on the 12th at Brown's Ranch Trailhead in Scottsdale. After splitting up during the hike, the wife never returned to their meeting location. Local authorities from various agencies responded to search for the missing woman. Shortly after 2100MST, local authorities found the missing woman who had succumbed to the heat.
Strong winds resulted in widespread areas of blowing dust. Spotters reported visibility at or below 1/4 mile at Tacna, Ligurta and Wenden.
Streets and highways became flooded and some road closures were reported after rainfall rates exceeded 2 inches per hour in the heaviest storms. One spotter in East Mesa had a total of 2.50 inches.

A large dead tree fell through a brick wall in a apartment complex in the area of Rural and Baseline Roads in Tempe as line of strong showers and storms associated with a cold front moved through. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
A wind gust of 66 mph was measured at the Imperial County Airport.
A wind gust of 72 mph was measured at the El Centro Naval Air Facility.
A Yuma Proving Ground Station measured a wind gust of 61 mph.
A mesonet station in Paradise Valley measured a wind gust of 61 mph.
A mesonet station near Tonto Basin measured a wind gust of 59 mph.
A large uprooted tree broke a main water pipe, causing water to be cut off to an apartment complex located in the area of North 32nd Street and East Shea Blvd. No injuries were reported.
Shingles taken off roof along with large tree down were reported in the area of Miami. No injuries were reported.
Northbound lanes of Alma School were blocked from Elliot to the Western Canal due to a tree in the roadway in Chandler. No injuries were reported.
A video posted onto Facebook showed wood frames blew down at a construction site near the Walmart in the city of Maricopa. No injuries were reported.
A wind gust of 59 mph was measured at the Yuma International Airport.
A very large uprooted tree fell near a house in Casa Grande. No injuries were reported.
A mesonet station located near Tortilla Flat measured a wind gust of 72 mph as a line of showers and storms quickly moved eastward through the foothills north and east of Phoenix.
Seventy-six power poles were knocked down, cutting power to about 2500 customers. Thirty-five poles went down north of Salton City and forty-one poles went down south of Salton City.
A 66 mph wind gust was measured at the El Centro Naval Air Facility.
A 62 mph wind gust was measured at the Imperial County Airport.
A 60 mph wind gust was measured at the El Centro Naval Air Facility.
The Globe Sheriffs Office reported 3/4 inch diameter hail. Trained spotters in Globe estimated wind gusts between 40 and 50 mph.
A total of 1.20 inches of rain fell in 18 minutes, resulting in street flooding. A trained spotter in Globe also had very heavy rain, with 1.36 inches in only 25 minutes.
Power poles and trees were reported down at Chandler Heights and Greenfield roads, as well as Ocotillo and Higley and at Ocotillo and Power roads.
An overhead sign was blown down by strong winds in the northbound lanes of South Rural Road near US-60 in Tempe. No injuries were reported.
A four-inch diameter tree limb snapped in the area of 50th street and Chandler Boulevard in Ahwatukee. No injuries were reported.
Snowfall of 7 inches was reported in the area of Sunflower, AZ.
Trained spotter reported 5 inches about 11 miles south-southeast of Globe.
Nineteenth Avenue from Desert Hills Drive to Irvine Road along Skunk Creek in Carefree was closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
North Old Stage Road at the Cave Creek River crossing was closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Video submitted on social media showed Circle Mountain Road inundated by a fast-running wash. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Gauge at Casandro Wash in Wickenburg registered flows going above alarm stage, which is 2.2 feet, at 20:03 MST. The flow reached a peak of 4.76 feet (343 cfs) at 20:30 MST and went below flood stage by 22:03 MST. This likely contributed to flooding along the inflow to Casandro Dam as well as small road crossings that intersect the wash. No damages or injuries were reported.
Portions of Jack Burden Rd in Wickenburg closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Portions of Vulture Mine Rd in Wickenburg closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Tonopah Salome Highway between 327th Drive and 315th Avenue was closed due to overflow from the Hassayampa River. No damages or injuries were reported.
Baseline Rd between Johnson Rd and 331st Ave was closed due to flooding from the overflow of the Hassayampa River. No damages or injuries were reported.

Patton Road between 293rd Ave and Douglas Ranch Rd was closed due to flooding from the overflow of the Hassayampa River. A Maricopa County Flood Control District Gauge located 11 miles upstream registered flows going above alarm stage, which is 9.0 feet, at 21:50 MST on 3/15, peaking at 9.81 feet (2011 cfs) at 23:30 MST. The flow went below alarm stage at 10:58 MST on 3/16. No damages or injuries were reported.
Old Stage Rd Northbound at New River Rd was closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
The Yuma Auxiliary Airfield Station measured a 60 mph gust.

According to the Maricopa County DOT, McKellips Road between Alma School Road and SR 202 was closed due to flooding from the Salt River beginning on the 7th and continued into April. Timing based on water releases from Granite Reef Dam.

According to MCDOT, the unbridged Salt River crossing along 67th Avenue between Broadway Road and Southern Avenue was closed due to flooding beginning on the 12th and continued into April. Timing based on water releases from Granite Reef Dam.

According to MCDOT, the unbridged Gila River crossing along El Mirage Road between Southern Avenue and Indian Springs Road was closed due to flooding beginning on the 14th and continued into April. Timing based on water releases from Granite Reef Dam.

Live broadcast showed a utility truck, with two men inside the vehicle, washed off of East Rockaway Hills Drive, due to elevated flow in the Cave Creek Basin, requiring a swift water rescue. The two men were safely rescued.

Patton Road was closed due to flooding from the Hassayampa River. A Maricopa County Flood Control District Gauge located 11 miles upstream registered flows rising above alarm stage, which is 9 feet, at 22:18 PM MST on 3/21, peaking at 12.25 feet (7903 cfs) at 12:24 PM MST on 3/22. The water flow went below alarm stage at 3:07 PM MST on 3/23. No damages or injuries were reported.
Tonopah Salome Highway was closed due to flooding from the Hassayampa River. No damages or injuries were reported.
A video posted onto social media showed water from the Hassayampa River flowing along Baseline Road, causing its closure. No damages or injuries were reported.

Desert Hills Drive and 19th Ave were both closed due to flooding from Skunk Creek. A Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gauge showed water levels briefly rising above alarm stage, which is 2.2 feet. No damages or injuries were reported.

According to MCDOT, the unbridged Salt River crossing along Gilbert Road between Thomas Road and SR 87 was closed due to flooding beginning on the 14th and continued into April. Timing based on water releases from Granite Reef Dam.

Two people became stranded on top of their vehicle in the Salt River along 91st Avenue near Baseline Road after attempting to cross through the flooded roadway. The initial call for help occurred on the 17th around 1845 MST. They were safely rescued by the fire department via helicopter. No injuries were reported. Event timing is based on releases from Granite Reef Dam.

Buckeye Fire Department performed a water rescue at the unbridged Gila River crossing along El Mirage Road between Southern Avenue and Indian Springs Road on the 18th. The exact details surrounding the water rescue are unknown. The road had been closed since the 14th due to the elevated flow in the river. Event timing is based on releases from Granite Reef Dam.

Maricopa County Sheriff's deputies received a call around 1145 MST on the 18th of a reported drowning after an 81-year-old man fell out of his kayak and didn't resurface. The incident occurred near the Pebble Beach area along the Salt River. Other kayakers on the river pulled the man out and administered first aid but were not successful. The man was pronounced dead at the scene. Approximately 20 minutes later, a family kayaking downstream on the Salt River near the Phon D Sutton Recreation Area had to be rescued after their kayak capsized. The family managed to stay afloat by holding onto some bushes and trees. All of the family members were safely rescued via helicopter by the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office. Ongoing dam releases were resulting in strong currents in the river at the time of these incidents. Event timing is based on downstream Granite Reef Dam releases.

A man was swept away after attempting to walk through the flooded unbridged El Mirage Road crossing that goes through the normally dry Gila River between Southern Avenue and Indian Springs Road. The man was walking through the water while carrying his bicycle when he was swept away on the 17th. The man was successfully rescued with no injuries reported. Event timing is based on Granite Reef Dam releases.

Two people kayaking on the Salt River approaching the Phon D Sutton Recreation Area became separated before one of them capsized on the 19th. The capsized kayaker was able to hold onto trees while the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office worked to rescue him via helicopter. The man was safely rescued with no injuries reported. Ongoing dam releases were resulting in strong currents in the river at the time. Event timing is based on downstream Granite Reef Dam releases.

Two people were rescued after driving around road closure barricades and attempting to drive through a flooded roadway with a recreational vehicle. While attempting to cross the flooded roadway, the recreational vehicle was swept off the road. The incident occurred around 2100 MST on the 30th at the unbridged El Mirage Road crossing that goes through the normally dry Gila River between Southern Avenue and Indian Springs Road. The two people were safely rescued by the fire department via helicopter. No injuries were reported. Event timing is based on Granite Reef Dam releases.
According to MCDOT, the unbridged Agua Fria River crossing along Lower Buckeye Road between 127th Avenue and 4th Street was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.

According to MCDOT, the low water crossing along Honda Bow Road between 7th Avenue and 9th Avenue was closed due to flooding from Skunk Creek. A downstream Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gauge showed water levels briefly reaching alarm stage, which is 2.2 feet. No damages or injuries were reported.

Lake levels at Bartlett Lake quickly rose during the overnight hours Thursday night into Friday morning on the 16th-17th. Levels reportedly rose 10 feet during the overnight hours, leaving at least two camp trailers submerged in several feet of water. No injuries were reported.

According to the Maricopa County DOT, McKellips Road between Alma School Road and SR 202 remained closed due to flooding from the Salt River beginning on March 7th and continuing through April. Timing based on water releases from Granite Reef Dam.

According to MCDOT, the unbridged Salt River crossing along 67th Avenue between Broadway Road and Southern Avenue was closed due to flooding beginning on March 12th and continuing into April. End timing estimated based on upstream FCDMC stream gauge at 51st Avenue.

According to MCDOT, the unbridged Gila River crossing along El Mirage Road between Southern Avenue and Indian Springs Road was closed due to flooding beginning on March 14th and continuing into April. End timing based on upstream FCDMC stream gauge along the Gila River at 116th Avenue.

According to MCDOT, the unbridged Salt River crossing along Gilbert Road between Thomas Road and SR 87 was closed due to flooding beginning on March 14th and continuing into April. The unbridged Gilbert Road crossing sustained heavy damage due to the high flows in the river, keeping the road closed after waters had receded. End timing based on water releases from Granite Reef Dam.

Two men paddle boarding down the Salt River were caught in an undercurrent near 19th Avenue and Broadway on the 9th. They became stuck in the undercurrent around 1000MST and began yelling for help before disappearing under the water. The bodies of the two men were recovered about a week later on the 15th and 16th. Flow in the Salt River was unusually high at the time due to continued upstream releases from Granite Reef Dam. Start time based on continued releases from Granite Reef Dam.

Water being released from Painted Rock Dam traveled down the Gila River, flooding several low water crossings between the dam and the Yuma County line. This led to the closures of Poco Dinero Road between Painted Rock Dam Road and Saddle Road as well as Rocky Point Road between Hyder Road and Painted Rock Dam Road.

Water being released from Painted Rock Dam continued to travel down the Gila River through Yuma County, flooding numerous unbridged river crossings. According to the Yuma County Sheriff's Office, numerous unbridged roads across the Gila River were closed due to flooding going into the last week of April. These road closures persisted into the month of May as elevated flows continued in the Gila River. The USGS gauge along the Gila River near Dateland show the gauge climbing above action stage (8 feet) on April 22nd. By April 30th, the USGS gauge along the Gila River near Dome began to respond as flow in the river continued to gradually travel downstream.
A 63 mph gust was measured at Imperial County Airport.
A mesonet station at Fish Creek Mountains measured a 59 mph gust.
A 67 mph gust was measured at the El Centro Naval Air Facility.
Semi truck rolled over along SR-86, just south of Salton City, injuring the driver. The two southbound lanes on the highway were blocked. Winds at the time estimated to be 35-45 mph.
SR-86 closed from the Riverside County line to Poe Road due to dust and strong winds. Caltrans reported near zero visibility near SR-86 and SR-78. No damages or injuries were reported.
Running washes lead to the closure of North Vulture Mine Road in Wickenburg. No damages or injuries were reported.
Saguaro tree uprooted in downtown Wickenburg. Winds were estimated at around 50 mph. No injuries were reported.
A 61 mph gust was measured at the Imperial County Airport.

Carport was ripped off of a mobile home, located in the area of Broadway and Lindsay Rd in Mesa, during the early afternoon hours, likely due to a dust devil. Awning was then blown back the other direction during the early evening hours likely from an outflow boundary moving through. Winds were estimated at approximately 50 mph. No injuries were reported.

Continued releases from Painted Rock Dam led to prolonged elevated flows traveling down the Gila River. As a result of this, several downstream low water crossings between the dam and the Yuma County line remained impassable due to flooding. This led to the closures of Poco Dinero Road between Painted Rock Dam Road and Saddle Road as well as Rocky Point Road between Hyder Road and Painted Rock Dam Road continuing through the month of May. Any damage sustained to these roads due to the prolonged elevated flow in the Gila River is unknown.

Continued releases from Painted Rock Dam led to prolonged elevated flows traveling down the Gila River through Yuma County. As a result, numerous downstream unbridged river crossings in Yuma County remained impassable due to flooding. These unbridged crossings remained closed through the month of May. According to local media reports, Yuma County Public Works reported that 14 unbridged crossings, which include Roll Road (paved) and 13 dirt roads, sustained damage due to the prolonged elevated flows in the river.
A strong dust devil impacted the Sierra Leone Mobile Home Park in Apache Junction, damaging several car ports and causing storage sheds to roll over.

Visibility of less than 1/8 mile reported in dense blowing dust due to thunderstorm outflow winds in the area of Hazeldine Road and Waverly Drive in Casa Grande. No accidents or injuries were reported.
Visibility of around 1/4 mile reported in dense blowing dust from thunderstorm outflow winds at the intersection of Meridian and Ray Rd. No accidents or injuries were reported.

Approximately a dozen downed power lines were reported along Barnes Road between Fuqua and Stanfield Roads in Stanfield, causing the road to be closed down for multiple days. Timing estimated from radar. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Visibility of 1/4 mile or less reported in Arizona City due to dense blowing dust from thunderstorm outflow winds. No accidents or injuries were reported.
A Union Pacific Railroad Mesonet observing site located just northwest of Eloy measured a 60 mph wind gust.
Visibility of less than 1/4 mile reported in the area of North Linnet Road in Casa Grande due to dense blowing dust from thunderstorm outflow winds. No accidents or injuries were reported.
A 61 mph wind gust was measured at the Ak-Chin Regional Airport.
Near zero visibility reported along State Route 347 near mile marker 183 due to dense blowing dust from thunderstorm outflow winds. No accidents or injuries were reported.
Broken roof tiles were observed near the area of US-60 in Gold Canyon. Wind gusts were estimated between 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Visibility of near zero observed in the intersection of Interstate 10 with State Route 347 due to dense blowing dust from thunderstorm outflow winds. No accidents or injuries were reported.
Visibility of 1/4 mile or less observed at Mesa Gateway Airport due to dense blowing dust from thunderstorm outflow winds. No accidents or injuries were reported.
Large tree limbs down in the area of East Lehi Road and North Terrace Circle in Mesa. Wind gusts were estimated at between 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
A house located in the area of East Lehi Road and North Pioneer in Mesa sustained roof damage to the garage. Winds were estimated between 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Significant wind damage centered around West Ingram and North Center Streets in Mesa. Five apartment complexes sustained roof damage. A large number of trees, block walls and other structures sustained damage. Wind gusts were estimated between 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Large tree limbs down in the area of East Nance Street and North Horne in Mesa. Wind gusts were estimated between 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.

A large pine tree with an estimated trunk diameter of 2-3 feet was knocked over in an apartment complex located in the are West Thunderbird Road in Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
A mesonet station located in the Sunnyslope neighbor of Phoenix measured a 61 mph gust.
A 63 mph gust was measured at the Scottsdale Municipal Airport.

Multiple downed trees with estimated diameter of 6-8 inches as well as a downed saguaro tree were reported in the area of I-17 and Happy Valley Road in Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated between 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
A large tree was knocked over in Sun City near 108th Ave and Thunderbird Road. Diameter of trunk estimated to be 2-3 ft. Wind gusts were estimated between 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
A large uprooted was reported in the area of 64th street and Osborn Road in Scottsdale. Wind gusts were estimated between 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Multiple trees down along the area of North Frank Lloyd Wright Boulevard and North 90th street in Scottsdale. One tree snapped in half with the largest tree diameter estimated to be a foot. Winds were estimated near 60 mph. No injuries were reported.

A mobile home park located in the area of North Mesa Drive and East McKellips Road in Mesa suffered widespread damage with the awnings from roofs and carports ripped apart. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Video showed multiple homes along the area of East Juniper Street and Pasadena in Mesa suffered roof damage. One home suffered damage to the garage door. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.

A large tree was down in the area of West Jomax Road and I-17. The tree toppled on top of a car. Diameter of the tree estimated at two feet. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Several homes along the area of North Mesa Drive and East McKellips Road in Mesa suffered roof damage. In addition to the damaged homes, a block wall was damaged and a downed tree estimated at two feet in diameter. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Large tree down estimated to be 1.5 feet in diameter at the area of West Lakeview Road and North 93rd Avenue in Peoria. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Large tree down in the area of 7th Street and Bell Road in Phoenix. Diameter of tree estimated to be about a foot. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Large tree branch down in the area of East Boston Street and South Santan Village Parkway in Gilbert. Tree branch is estimated to be three inches in diameter, breaking the windows of parked car. Wind gusts were estimated to be 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
An overhead street sign was blown down in the area of Pinal Avenue and Florence Boulevard in Casa Grande. Wind gusts were estimated around 55 mph. No injuries were reported.

A tree, with three separate trunks estimated to be 1-2 feet in diameter toppled and damaged a cinderblock wall along the area of West Loma Verde Avenue and West Acacia Drive in Eloy. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.

A couple of large trees down in the area of Lehi Road between North Mesa Drive and North Horne in Mesa. One of the tree toppled over a fence. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Approximately 9 tractor trailer rigs were blown over along I-10 near Vicksburg Rd in Vicksburg Junction. This occurred at two to three locations from milepost 41 to milepost 47 with both directions of traffic affected - especially westbound. Time estimated from first 911 call and radar. Wind gusts were estimated at 60 mph. According to a local news report, five people were hurt with two of them sustaining serious injuries.

A lightning strike sparked a fire in a tree farm located in the area of Ralston and Peters & Nall Roads southwest of Maricopa. The fire burned for nearly 24 hours after the lightning strike. No property damage nor injuries were reported with this fire.

A large uprooted tree caused a shed to bank upward at Cindy Rose Alterations in the Yuma Foothills. Wind gusts were estimated at between 50-55 mph based on nearby observations. Timing based on radar. No injuries were reported.
A 66 mph wind gust was report at the Imperial County Airport.
A 59 mph wind gust was measured at the El Centro Naval Air Facility.

Strong and gusty winds, along with heavy rain rolled through parts of  Yuma and San Luis. Arizona Public Service reported 26 power poles were knocked down in San Luis with seven main lines impacted. Trees were uprooted and caused property damage. At the Yuma airport, winds were clocked at 44 mph.

A 73-year-old man went on a bike ride in the Sun City Festival area around 1130MST on the 16th before experiencing a flat tire about an hour into his ride. He then called his wife and agreed to walk and meet her at a nearby fire department on Wagner Complex Drive so she could pick him up. His wife then called 911 after he didn't show up. Police and Buckeye Fire Department searched for the man and found his body in the desert less than a mile from the meeting location where he was planning to meet his wife. The Maricopa County Office of the Medical Examiner determined that his death was due to the heat. Temperatures during the early afternoon hours in this area were around 107-110 degrees.

Video as well as pictures showed several trees were damaged along the general between North Cooper Road and South Gilbert Road in Gilbert. Some trees had tree limbs broken while other trees were uprooted. Wind gusts were estimated between 55-60 mph based on radar estimates. No injuries were reported.

A parked semi-truck was blown over in the area of West Monaco Boulevard and South Saxon Road in Arizona City. Given that the truck was parked, it was likely that it was empty and thus was more likely to be blown over by sub-severe winds, which were estimated to be at around 50 mph. No injuries were reported.
A 70 mph wind gust was measured at the Gila Bend Air Force Auxiliary Field.

Broadcast footage showed several large trees uprooted, which caused property damage along Skyline Drive in the San Tan Valley area. A social media video footage showed what was likely a severe microburst hitting the area. There was a social media picture of a power pole leaning at about a 30 degree angle. Winds were estimated at between 60-70 mph. No injuries were reported.

Several broken tree limbs were blocking the roadway on Ellsworth Road about 1/4 mile north of Elliot Road in Mesa. Wind gusts were estimated at between 45-50 mph based on radar and nearby observations. No injuries were reported.

Roof panels, tree limbs, as well as some trees ranging between 7 to 18 inches in diameter were knocked down on the road in the area of South 86th street and East Broadway Road in Mesa. Wind gusts were estimated at between 45-50 mph based on radar and nearby stations. No injuries were reported.
A mesonet station located at the Phoenix International Raceway in Avondale measured a 68 mph gust.
Visibility down to as low as a few hundred feet was reported along I-8 west of Sentinel due to dense blowing dust from thunderstorm outflow. No accidents or injuries were reported.
Highway 177 north of Desert Center closed due to significant flooding between approximately Mile Markers 13 to 18. No damages or injuries were reported.

events.cz_name: IMPERIAL COUNTY EXCEPT THE LOWER COLORADO RIVER VALLEY
events.event_narrative: The visibility was reported as low as 1/4 mile at Imperial Airport. Spotters and other sources across Imperial County reported low visibilities due to blowing dust and sand associated with strong winds.
Images and videos showed multiple large trees uprooted at the City Hall in Apache Junction. No injuries were reported.

Multiple unbridged areas along SR 111 between Niland and North Shore were impacted due to flash flooding. Flash flooding impacts spanned along this highway in Imperial and Riverside Counties. According to local media, there were at least 10 reports of vehicles that became stuck along the highway and needed assistance from Imperial County Fire Department. No injuries were reported.
A mobile home at Lost Dutchman RV Resort had most of its roof peeled back due to damaging winds. No injuries were reported.
A 58 mph wind gust was measured at a mesonet station located just northwest of Casa Grande.
A wind gust of 64 mph was measured at the Ak-Chin Regional Airport.
Visibility less than 1/4 mile reported along Bowlin Road in Maricopa from dense blowing dust due to thunderstorm outflow winds. No accidents or injuries were reported.
A 74 mph wind gust was measured along the area of Sunland Gin Road and Kramer Lane in Arizona City.
A 60 mph wind gust was measured at a mesonet station located along State Route 230 just west of Maricopa.
A 59 mph wind gust was measured at a mesonet station located in the area of North Highland Drive and East Lamar Road in Paradise Valley.

A couple of mesquite trees, estimated at 8-10 diameter, were blown over in the area of E Jefferson Street between 10th and 11th street in downtown Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated to be up to 65 mph. No injuries were reported.
A 65 mph wind gust was measured from a mesonet station located along the area of South 16th street and East Roeser Road in Phoenix.
A quarter mile visibility was reported at Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport from dense blowing dust due to thunderstorm outflow winds. No accidents or injuries were reported.
A 73 mph wind gust was measured at Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport.
A 59 mph wind gust was measured at a mesonet station located along the area of South 43rd Avenue and West Lower Buckeye Road in Phoenix.
A 65 mph wind gust was measured at a mesonet station located at the Phoenix International Raceway in Avondale.
A 58 mph wind gust was measured at a mesonet station located in the area of South Avondale Boulevard and West Coldwater Springs Boulevard in Avondale.

A large downed 20 year old Mesquite Tree was reported at North Crooked Stick Road in Anthem. The downed tree was blocking the road and sitting on a car. Wind gusts were estimated at around 60 mph. No injuries were reported.
A 62 mph wind gust was measured at Phoenix Deer Valley Airport.
A 58 mph wind gust was measured at a mesonet station located along West Britton Avenue in Glendale.
A 58 mph wind gust was measured at a mesonet station located in the area of North 107th Avenue just south of Interstate 10.
A 58 mph wind gust was measured at Luke Air Force Base.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Gauge along Skunk Tank Wash near the intersection of Desert Hills Drive and North 7th Avenue reported flows rising to above alarm stage, which is 4.2 feet, at 22:21 MST. The flow peaked at 7.09 feet (674 cfs), which is above the flood stage of 7.00 feet, at 22:49 MST. The flow fell below alarm stage at 23:43 MST. The elevated water flow caused the closure of Desert Hills Drive between 19th and 15th Avenues due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.

Flash flooding was reported in Salton City along Seaview Drive, which has a low water crossing through a wash. According to local media reports, a mother and her two children had to be rescued after their vehicle became stuck in a wash. No injuries were reported.
A social media video showed that a low water crossing along Marina Drive in Salton City was impassable due to flooding. No injuries were reported.
CHP reported flash flooding near Orchard Road and Edwards Road. No injuries were reported.
A water rescue was reported in the intersection of West Joy Ranch Road and North Pioneer Road in Anthem due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Water rescue performed on East Cloud Road just east of North 7th Street in Anthem as person was rescued from vehicle due to flooding. The vehicle, a Ford F150, was swept away by the flood waters.

Video uploaded by the Daisy Mountain Fire Department Station 142 in Anthem showed several inches of flowing water along a street within the station's jurisdiction. No damages or injuries were reported.

Downed powerlines were reported along the area of South 20th street to South 32nd Street and East Elwood street to East Roeser Road in Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated to be up to 65 mph. No injuries were reported.

Downed powerlines were reported along the area of North 59th Avenue to North 51st Avenue and West Bethany Home Road to West Missouri Avenue in Glendale. Wind gusts were estimated to be at approximately 60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Downed powerlines were reported along the area of South Priest Drive to South Hardy Drive and West 1st Street to West University Drive in Tempe. Wind gusts were estimated to be up to 65 mph. No injuries were reported.
Downed powerlines were reported along the area of McKinley St to Pima St and 31st Ave to 23rd Ave in Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated to be up to 65 mph. No injuries were reported.
Downed powerlines were reported along the area of Auto Drive to Western Avenue and Litchfield Road to 5th Street in Goodyear. Wind gusts were estimated at around 60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Downed powerlines were reported along the area of Yuma Road to Broadway Road and 231st Avenue to Airport Road in Buckeye. Wind gusts were estimated at around 60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Visibility of approximately a quarter mile reported along the area of West Val Vista Road and Interstate 10 in Casa Grande from dense blowing dust due to thunderstorm outflow winds. No accidents or injuries were reported.
A peak wind gust of 66 mph was measured at KIPL. However, the station stopped reporting during the event, so it's unknown if stronger gusts occurred later in the day.

A gas station canopy located on the corner of Adams Avenue and Imperial Avenue fell down due to strong winds. Additional reports throughout the Imperial Valley included downed trees, power poles, and light poles with the exact location of these occurrences unknown. No injuries were reported. Timing estimated based on peak wind gust at KIPL.
According to Caltrans, Highway 98 near Ocotillo was closed due to flash flooding. No injuries were reported.
Visibility dropped down to as low as 100 feet at times along I-8 near Tacna due to blowing dust. No accidents or injuries were reported.
A 69 mph gust was measured at KNYL.
Visibility dropped down to 1/4 mile at KNYL. Nearby in the Somerton area, emergency management reported visibility below 1/8 mile due to dense blowing dust. No accidents or injuries were reported.

Several downed power poles were reported on Highway 95 between Pacific Avenue and Araby Road. There were additional instances across the Yuma area of down power lines and downed power poles along with downed trees. No injuries were reported.

Multiple instances of wind damage were reported along several different roads near the Tacna area, including Avenue 16, Avenue 31, Avenue 36, and Avenue 42. Along Avenues 31 and 36, railroad crossing signals were toppled or damaged. Power lines were reported down along Avenues 16 and 42. Awnings were also destroyed on RVs in the Welton area. Timing estimated based on nearby observations. No injuries were reported.
Water rescue reported along the intersection of North New River Road and North 67th Avenue in Anthem due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.

A damaged mobile home awning laid on the road of North 103 Avenue between West Olive Avenue and West Northern Avenue in Glendale. Timing estimated from radar. Wind gusts were estimated at around 60 mph. No injuries were reported.
A lightning strike sparked a fire half an acre in size along the TV towers in South Mountain in Phoenix. Firefighters were able to extinguish fire successfully with structural damage reported.
Barnes Road from Stanfield Road to Murphy Road closed due to Green Wash running. No damages or injuries were reported.
Massive 2-4 foot diameter tree fell across a few cars in the area of North 75th Avenue and West Indian School Road in Glendale. Wind gusts were estimated at around 60 mph. No injuries were reported.
A palm tree fell and landed on top of a car in the area of South 40th street and East Van Buren Street. Wind gusts were estimated of up to 70 mph. No injuries were reported.
A large uprooted tree in the area of South 35th Avenue and West Vineyard Road in Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated of up to 65 mph. No injuries were reported.
Photos of large tree branches blocking road in the Glenarm Farms Neighborhood in Avondale. Wind gusts were estimated of up to 60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Photos showing several large uprooted trees in the city of Maricopa. Wind gusts were estimated of up to 60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Large uprooted tree in the area of North Central Avenue and East Northern Avenue in Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated of up to 60 mph. No injuries were reported.
A palm tree caught on fire due to a lightning strike in the area of North Timberland Drive located in the Gainey Ranch area of Scottsdale. No injuries were reported.

Approximately 12 mobile homes sustained severe roof/shingle damage at the Coyote Ranch mobile home park. Nearby along Fortuna Road, a carport awning was destroyed with part of the awning blocking much of the roadway. Timing and wind magnitude estimated based on nearby observations. No injuries were reported.
A couple of tractor trailers were blown over along I-8 near the Glamis Dunes. No injuries were reported.
A large tree was blown down near El Centro Street and Haskell Road. No injuries were reported.
Power poles were reported down near Evan Hewes Highway. No injuries were reported.
A 58 mph gust was recorded at KBLH.

A 34-year-old woman went hiking at the Deem Hills Recreation Area around 0830MST when temperatures were in the low 90s, according to a nearby observation. She was then reported missing around noon after failing to return from her hike. Midday temperatures in the area were around 100-105 degrees. Family and friends searched for the missing hiker with firefighters and police. Her body was later discovered around 1700MST in a remote area near a trail. According to the Maricopa County Office of the Medical Examiner, heat was a contributing factor in the hiker's death.
Three downed power poles along West Miller Road about two miles west of Highway 347. Timing based on radar. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Downed power poles near the area Maricopa Rd and Highway 347 just west of I-10. Traffic signals were out leading to significant traffic impacts. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Several large trees estimated to be up to 1 foot in diameter were uprooted in the area of West Indian School Road and North Litchfield Road in Goodyear. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Power lines were snapped in the area of North 17th Street and East Oak Street in Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 65-70 mph. No injuries were reported.

Giant 60 year old pine was uprooted, taking out two block walls as well as a couple power lines in the area of North 66th Street and East Oak Street in Scottsdale. Wind gusts were estimated at 65-70 mph. No injuries were reported.

A very large uprooted tree fell onto the roof of a home located along the area of North 40th Street and Indian School Road in Phoenix. Tree was estimated to be 90 feet tall with its root system at 13 feet in diameter. Winds were estimated at approximately 65-70 mph. No injuries were reported.

More than 100 trees downed in the city of Scottsdale parks, including 60 in the area of Vista Del Camino and El Dorado Parks. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 65-70 mph. No injuries were reported.

Multiple downed power poles and on top of houses in the area of Recker Road between East McDowell Road and East McKellips Road in Mesa. Multiple downed trees were also observed. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 80 mph. No injuries were reported.

Numerous reports of considerable damage at Falcon Field Airport from a severe microburst. Around 25 airplanes, mostly Cessna small aircraft, were damaged or destroyed, with some flipped over. One aviation flight school lost one third of their fleet, but it is unknown how many aircraft that amounts to. A few pilots reported that even planes with proper tie-downs broke free, with wind eyelets snapping and chains breaking as the planes likely tried to become airborne. Numerous hangars suffered significant damage, with around 90 hangar doors damaged or destroyed. Two World War II era hangars were damaged, with one losing its roof. Another hangar had an entire side wall shorn off. There were several downed trees around the airport, as well as damages to some other airport infrastructure and property, like fencing. A news report nearly three months later stated repairs are still being done and the total damages at the airport is around $7.2 million. An ASOS at Falcon Field Airport did not measure peak wind gusts from this storm due to a loss of power at the airport. Thus, based on damages, winds were estimated around 90 mph. No injuries were reported.
Multiple large trees were snapped and/or uprooted in the area of North Power and East McKellips Roads in Mesa. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 80 mph. No injuries were reported.

An AC unit was blown off the roof of a home located in the area of East Brown and North Power Roads in Mesa and landed on two brand new cars. The unit shattered the windshield of one car and dented the other car. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 80 mph. No injuries were reported.
Home weather station located at 2915 East Minton Road in Mesa recorded a peak wind gust of 81 mph.
Large tree approximately 9-11 inches in diameter was uprooted in 8534 East Halifax Circle in Mesa. Wind gusts were estimated at around 60 mph. No injuries were reported.
A 60 foot pine tree was uprooted and toppled over a home causing damage to the patio roof. Wind gusts were estimated at between 65-70 mph. No injuries were reported.
Tree limb of approximately 6-8 inches in diameter was snapped from a large tree in the area of North Miller Road and East McDowell Road in Scottsdale. No injuries were reported.

Severe damage occurred at Zaharis Elementary School located at the intersection of East McKellips Road and North Ellsworth Road in Mesa. Significant water damage occurred with several ceiling tiles ripped off as well as downed trees and debris across the campus. School was forced to close down for approximately a week due to the heavy damage. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 80 mph. No injuries were reported.

Downed power lines resulting the closure of North Cox Road between West Randolph Road and West McCartney Road in Casa Grande were reported. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Downed powerlines were reported in the area of North Pinal Avenue and West Val Vista Boulevard in Casa Grande. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
State Route 88 between mileposts 229 and 242 southwest of Roosevelt Lake was closed due to flooding and rockslides, making the road impassable. No injuries were reported.

The overflowing from Weekes Wash lead to several road closures in Apache Junction including: Tomahawk Rd. (4th Ave to Junction St.); 4th Ave. (Tomahawk Rd. to Cactus Rd.); Junction St. (Tomahawk Rd. to Wickiup Rd.); and Scenic St. (Vista Rd. to Wickiup Rd.). No damages nor injuries were reported.
Nickel size hail reported in the area of East Thomas Road and Loop 101 in Scottsdale. No damages nor injuries reported.
Spring Creek Wash in Roosevelt was running about 3 feet deep. No damages nor injuries were reported.
A couple of mobile homes sustained severe roof damage in the area of East University Drive and Loop 202 in Mesa. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 80 mph. No injuries were reported.
Large tree uprooted in the area of Lindsay Road and East McKellips Road in Mesa. Wind gusts were estimated at 65-70 mph. No injuries were reported.
Video showed hailstones up to one inch in diameter in the Mountain Bridge Neighbor in Mesa located just east of Loop 202. No damages or injuries were reported.

Video showed the roof from a home taken completely apart, flying approximately 100 feet away. Video also showed multiple large trees within the vicinity uprooted. The damage took place in a neighborhood complex located along North Recker Road just north of East McKellips Road in Mesa. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 80 mph. No injuries were reported.

Photo evidence showed damage to the roofing system as the satellite antenna dish of a home located at 2139 North Recker Road in Mesa. Hailstones were estimated to be up to one inch in diameter. No injuries were reported.

Large trees uprooted along with ceramic tiles on rooftops damaged in the Mountain Bridge Neighborhood located near East McKellips Road in Mesa. Wind gusts were estimated at approximately 80 mph. No injuries were reported.
Semi truck flipped and on its side due to strong winds. Winds estimated at 60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Several power poles were reported knocked over and nearly in the road along Highway 111 between Aten and Worthington Roads. Winds estimated at 60 mph. No injuries were reported.
A semi-truck rolled over on Highway 86 due to strong winds and blocked both lanes of traffic. Winds were estimated at 60 mph. No injuries were reported, but medical was called to the scene.
An incident report from California Highway Patrol said that multiple vehicles were stopped due to flooding on Highway 78. No injuries or damages were reported.
Virginia Drive was closed between 24th Street and 28th Street due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.

A video on social media showed a semi driving through a flooded low water crossing along SR 72 at Avenue 41 E with at least 6 inches of water flowing over the road. Timing was estimated from radar. No damage or injuries were reported.
An image on social media showed elevated flow within Tyson Wash through La Paz Valley, making a low water crossing impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.

Widespread 1 to 2 inches of radar estimated rain fell in Niland and areas just east into the Chocolate Mountains. A large area of considerable runoff flowed through Niland and the surrounding area, as evident in reports and before and after Sentinel2 satellite images, with upwards of 6 inches to 1 foot of flowing water in some areas, per photos and videos. Major flash flooding impacts were experienced. The East Highline Canal east of Niland, was overcome with flood waters and silt, mainly north of of Flowing Wells Rd. The overflowing canal was first reported a little after 1600PDT and only exacerbated the flooding. Several roads became impassable, unsafe, and subsequently closed due to flood water. At least a few cars became stuck in flood water leading to swift water rescues by land and air. The exact number of rescues is unknown. In Niland, several photos and videos showed flooded streets and yards, with water coming up to homes and businesses. There were a few reports of water entering homes, but it is unknown how many homes were impacted. Also impacted in the area was agriculture, as several fields had flood water moving through them. It is unknown the extent of any damages to the agricultural fields or the exact number. Sentinel2 satellite images showed evidence of all the disturbed earth, deposited mud and silt, through Niland, the agricultural fields and surrounding areas. In a statement by Imperial Irrigation District, the impacts to East Highline Canal resulted in a delay of 133 water deliveries. Also the O Lateral canal, which branches from East Highline canal, suffered structural damage. The main highway through the area, Hwy-111, was flooded in several locations, which hampered relief efforts. The small town of Slab City, to the northeast of Niland, was cut off from the rest of the Imperial Valley due to the flooded roads. As a result of the significant impacts, the County of Imperial issued an emergency proclamation for additional and better resources. Red Cross assisted in relief and a couple shelters for evacuees were established. There were no injuries reported from this event and specifics on property and crop damage is unknown and thus grossly estimated.

Photos showed visibility dropped below 1/4 mile in blowing dust and sand along I-8 with winds gusting to 40 to 50 mph behind a strong outflow boundary. The strong gusts and reduced visibilities lasted for over 1 hour. No accidents were reported.

Multiple large trees were toppled on the campus of Imperial Valley College. The college also lost power, due to nearby downed powerlines, and sustained damage to their fiber optic network. This led to the closure of the school. Winds were estimated around 60 mph. No injuries were reported.

In the early afternoon, 6 hikers were 4 miles in on Spur Cross Trail when they became lost and ran out of water. The hikers' phones were also dead and had to borrow someone else's phone to call for help. After calling for help, first responders were able to rescue the hikers and airlift them off the trail. One hiker was taken to the hospital but did not survive. A Scottsdale Fire Captain said the individual died due to heat exhaustion and heat stroke. The Maricopa County Office of the Medical Examiner listed the primary cause of death as dehydration and heat exposure. Temperatures in the early afternoon were around 103-105 degrees.

A large palm tree fell directly on a man walking in Highline Park in Phoenix, killing him. There was a peak wind gust of 45 mph reported by a Citizen Weather Observer Site located nearby.
Ogilby Road closed between Interstate 8 and State Route 78 due to overflowing washes causing flooding on the road. No damages or injuries were reported.
State Route 98 closed between County Highway 2 and Brockman Road due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
State Route 111 closed between Mile Marker 55.7 and the Riverside County Line due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported along State Route 86 in the area of Red Earth Casino. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported in the area of State Route 111 and East Worthington Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported along East Aten Road between Dogwood Road and State Route 111. No damages or injuries were reported.

Box Canyon Road closed between Interstate 10 and the All-American Canal due to flooding causing light mud and debris flow. No damages were reported.

The New River USGS Gauge at the International Border in Calexico reported water levels peaking to 15.6 feet, which is just above minor flood stage. The rise to minor flood stage was generally gradual as water levels rose at a rate of 1 feet per hour according to the gauge data. The rising water levels caused damage to an improvement project being performed at the New River in Calexico with water overtopping the sheet piles. About 10 feet of standing water was estimated inside the sheet piles. This water overtopping caused a generator controlling the dewatering to flood and shutdown. The city of Calexico declared an emergency due to the damages that the high water levels caused to the project. According to an interview performed with a city councilmember  approximately two weeks after the incident, the damage cost estimate was at around 4 million dollars. No injuries were reported.
Avenue A by 28th Street was closed due to a storm drain shooting water up and causing the road to flood. No damages or injuries were reported.
East County 13th street was flooded at the intersection with Fortuna Wash due to water flowing along the wash. No damages or injuries were reported.
Union Pacific railroad crossing was closed on Fortuna Rd between Highway 95 and 24th St due to flooding and erosion. No damages or injuries were reported.
Dense blowing dust reduced the visibility to 1/4 mile at Riggs and Higley Roads.
One inch of rain in only 30 minutes.
Wind speed measured at 68 mph at Bush Highway and Usery Pass Road. According to radar, these storms were moving west at about 35 mph.

West Agate Road wad closed from South Olivine Road to South Amarillo Valley Road due to running washes with the road washed out at the intersection with South Amarillo Valley Road. No injuries were reported.
Flooding along San Carlos river just south of San Carlos.
West Sotol Road from South Quicksilver Road to South Amarillo Valley Road was closed due to running washes. No injuries were reported.
West Barnes Rd closed from Stanfield Road to North Pala Road due to running washes. No damages or injuries were reported.
Highway 238 initially closed from Mileposts 32-38 due to flooding. Approximately four hours later, the closure along the highway extended to Gila Bend. No damages or injuries were reported.

Numerous streets and highways reported flooded in Phoenix and Tempe. One spotter near Guadalupe and McClintock picked up 2 1/2 inches in just 45 minutes. One unofficial report near Baseline and I-10 included 3.75 inches from this storm. A roof of a charter school in Ahwatukee was reported to have collapsed from the accumulated rain water.
A record daily maximum rainfall of 1.30 inches was set at Sky Harbor Airport. Other reports of heavy rain included .90 inch in 20 minutes in Tempe, and 1.00 inch in 20 minutes near Wickenburg.
Visibility less than 1/4 mile was reported in Tacna, Ligurta and Wenden.
Strong winds resulted in a large Palo Verde tree toppling over onto a parked car sitting in a parking lot near Frye Road and Chandler Village Drive. No injuries were reported.
Dense blowing dust led to 1/4 mile visibility near I-10 and Riggs Road.
Dense blowing dust led to 1/4 mile visibility at the I-10 and Loop 202 interchange.
Dense blowing dust led to 1/4 mile visibility near Loop 202 and 40th Street.
Salome Road reported closed due to water over roadway. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Main road into the Joshua Tree NP, the Utah Trail road, was closed due to flooding.  More than 2 inches of rain fell across parts of the area with numerous roads closed in the surrounding areas. Pinto Basin road was also flooded.
Heavy rains, up to .75 inch in 30 minutes, were reported in Miami Gardens, leaving some streets flooded. Another spotter picked up a storm total of 1.20 inches.

Pilot reported sighting a brief funnel cloud. Thunderstorms were triggered by an old outflow boundary. The associated peak wind gusts were 28 knots at Sky Harbor and 39 knots at Scottsdale airport. One spotter near Ray and Priest roads picked up .5 inch in 20 minutes.

Strong winds resulted in damages to the mobile home at the NWS Cooperative Site located in Chiraco Summit. Damages included a metal awning and shingles stripped off. In addition, the exterior door to the utility room that faced the north-facing wall of the home was badly damaged. No injuries were reported.
Scottsdale airport recorded peak winds of 53 mph during thunderstorms. Winds at Sky Harbor airport reached as high as 39 mph and some tents at the Tempe Town Lake fireworks display were blown down.

Visual photos showed a weak landspout developed over an open field near the Casa Grande Mountains just south of Casa Grande, AZ from a thunderstorm cell moving over the area. The landspout lasted for about 8 minutes with no evidence of any damages or injuries.
Pinto Creek at highway 188 was reported to be filled, and Campaign Creek broke through a small berm at Roosevelt Lake Estates. One spotter at Roosevelt Resort had 1.5 to 2 inches of rain.
An accident on I-10 at milepost 45 was blamed on high winds and low visibility.
Washes and low spots flooded after very heavy rains struck the area.

The Maricopa County Flood Control District Gauge at Indian Bend Wash near Shea Boulevard reported water levels rising above alarm stage, which is 2 feet, at 3:30 am MST, peaking at around 2.31 feet (1055 cfs) at 6:00 am MST. Water levels dropped below alarm stage by 8:30 am MST. The intersection of North Scottsdale Road and Indian Bend Road was closed due to flooding from the elevated water levels from the wash. No damages or injuries were reported.

Large tree blown onto road leading to a road closure of Bennett Road from Even Hewes Highway to Ross Road. Imperial County Airport nearby reported peak wind gusts up to 35-40 mph. No injuries were reported.

A strong outflow from collapsing showers moving through the area resulted in strong winds across Parker Strip. The strong winds destroyed some sheds, with the metal roofing becoming entangled around a power pole, knocking power out. Based on the magnitude of the damage observed, wind gusts were estimated to be upwards of 50 mph. No injuries were reported.
Near zero visibility in blowing dust on I-10 in Casa Grande. There was also a traffic accident during the dust storm with one person transported to the hospital.

A wildfire named the Rose Fire developed about 5 miles southeast of Wickenburg, AZ along a river bed near U.S. Highway 60. The fire jumped on the other side of the highway, forcing its closure. The fire caused evacuations of people living along the homes situated nearby. At the end, the blaze destroyed 15 structures, seven which were primary residences, along with 12 vehicles, a horse trailer, and a recreational vehicle. In total, the fire consumed nearly 200 acres. No injuries were reported.

The Buckeye Municipal Airport measured a 61 mph gust from a virga shower that moved overhead. Nearby, in the community of Tartesso, a small shed was thrown far from a home onto a street. No injuries were reported.

Tents became airborne and large limbs fell from a tree in the center median of 107th Ave intersecting with Happy Valley Road in Surprise. Wind gusts were estimated at between 40-50 mph based on nearby observing sites. No injuries were reported.

A tree branch estimated to be between 1 to 1.5 inches in diameter snapped due to strong winds from outflow boundary near the intersection of 67th Avenue and Loop 101 in Glendale. Gusts were estimated at 40-50 mph based on nearby surface observations. No injuries were reported.

Palo verde tree uprooted due to strong winds from outflow boundary at the Fry's Supermarket parking lot located near the intersection of 43rd Avenue and Bell Road in Glendale. Wind gusts were estimated at 40-50 mph based on nearby surface observations.

Visibility at around 50 feet was observed in the area of West Val Vista Boulevard and I-10 in Casa Grande due to blowing dust from thunderstorm winds. No accidents nor injuries were reported.

Semi-truck was flipped by strong wind gusts and was blocking most of the EB lanes on I-10 near Desert Center, causing traffic to back up. Winds gusts were estimated upwards of 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Several downed Power lines in a squared area encompassing South Mountain Road to South Delaware Drive and West Southern Avenue to East Broadway Road in Apache Junction. Wind gusts were estimated upwards of 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Flooding on SR-87 Northbound near N Hashan Kehk Rd in Sacaton. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Power poles down near Buckeye Rd and 339th Ave west of Buckeye. Winds gusts were estimated upwards of 70 mph. No injuries were reported.

Significant damage observed to several homes and yards across the Sweetwater and West Phoenix Estates areas in Buckeye due. The damages reported included a sheet of metal that was lodged into a house wall, holes in house roofing, metal frame set swimming pool completely destroyed, and metal fencing panels torn down. Downed power poles in the area of Polk Street and 295th Avenue in Buckeye. Wind gusts were estimated upwards of 70 mph. No injuries were reported.

Mesonet stream gauge along Gilson Wash recorded an approximate 2.38 ft jump, impacting downstream low water crossings. No damages nor injuries were reported.

The Watch Fire began on the 10th before rapidly spreading during the afternoon of the 11th due to strong thunderstorm outflow winds in excess of 30-40 mph. The strong winds caused the fire to rapidly spread into southeast portions of San Carlos, destroying at least 21 homes and 13 auxiliary structures. The fire became 100 percent contained on the 17th after burning more than 2,000 acres. No injuries were reported.
A mesonet station located about 30 miles south of Gila Bend measured a 70 mph wind gust from thunderstorm downburst winds.

According to the Maricopa County Flood Control District Gauge located at Cruff Wash, water levels rose above the alarm level stage of 2.5 feet at around 1952MST and crested at 3.91 feet, which is above the bank full level stage of 3.88 feet, at around 2015MST. Water levels fell below alarm stage at around 2105MST. Based on the information of problem areas produced by the Maricopa County Flood Control District, flooding was likely along the low water crossing of Agua Caliente Road located above 2 miles downstream of the gauge. No damages nor injuries were reported.

The large uprooted trees caused significant damage to the Avia McCormick Ranch Apartment Complex as the downed trees destroyed a side roof, damaged vehicles, and blocked road access around the complex, forcing the Scottsdale Fire Department to evacuate several units as some residents were trapped inside. Wind gusts were estimated upwards of 70 mph. No injuries were reported.

A 73-year-old man went on a bike ride in the Sun City Festival area around 1130MST on the 16th before experiencing a flat tire about an hour into his ride. He then called his wife and agreed to walk and meet her at a nearby fire department on Wagner Complex Drive so she could pick him up. His wife then called 911 after he didn't show up. Police and Buckeye Fire Department searched for the man and found his body in the desert less than a mile from the meeting location where he was planning to meet his wife. The Maricopa County Office of the Medical Examiner determined that his death was due to the heat. Temperatures during the early afternoon hours in this area were around 107-110 degrees.

A 34-year-old woman went hiking at the Deem Hills Recreation Area around 0830MST when temperatures were in the low 90s, according to a nearby observation. She was then reported missing around noon after failing to return from her hike. Midday temperatures in the area were around 100-105 degrees. Family and friends searched for the missing hiker with firefighters and police. Her body was later discovered around 1700MST in a remote area near a trail. According to the Maricopa County Office of the Medical Examiner, heat was a contributing factor in the hiker's death.

Multiple vehicle collisions resulted in the closure of Sunland Gin Road from Battaglia Drive to Mountain View Avenue near Arizona City to due to dense blowing dust, with visibilities less than a quarter mile observed. No injuries were reported.
A 58 mph wind gust was measured at the Imperial County Airport.
Nearly two inches of rain caused streets in Florence to become flooded.
Winds snapped a power pole at Central and Butte Avenues.

A vehicle with 5 women was swept away as it was caught in raging flood waters along route 72, about a mile and a half southeast of Bouse. One woman died and her body was found about 7 miles away. An RV was also stranded by flood waters in the same wash at the same time.
Winds knocked a power line onto the street.
KBLH ASOS measured a peak wind gust of 58 mph.

Several semi-trucks (10 approximately) flipped over on I-10 between Desert Center and Indio from strong northerly crosswinds. Peak wind gusts of approximately 60 mph were estimated. At least 1 minor injury reported.
A 62 mph wind gust was measured at Blythe Airport.
A 63 mph wind gust was measured at Blythe Airport.
Power lines down near 7th Street and Northern.
Estimated gusts to about 58 mph. Another spotter in Globe had a measured gust of 45 mph at 4:55 pm MST.
Large hail was reported by employees at the Imperial Irrigation District.
Two short-lived funnel clouds observed in the area.

events.cz_name: IMPERIAL COUNTY EXCEPT THE LOWER COLORADO RIVER VALLEY
events.event_narrative: Strong winds, generally between 40 and 50 mph caused widespread areas of visibility less than 1/4 mile.
Power outage due to strong winds. Possible funnel cloud near mile marker 256 on highway 70.
Flooding reported on route 188. One spotter in Roosevelt observed one inch of rain in only 15 minutes.
About 1.1 inches fell in just 30 minutes at Chandler and McQueen. Some streets were flooded.
Strong winds reported at Brown and Mesa. Trees were damaged.

Several crashes on the Loop 202 were blamed on strong winds and rain. Power outages were reported after winds and rain moved through the East Valley. SRP reported about 3,000 customers were left without electricity...and APS reported 2,000 customers without power.
Strong winds reported by spotter.
Winds at Chandler Airport reached 50 knots as severe thunderstorms moved toward the west.
Five power poles blown down at Randolph and Eleven Mile Corner roads. A police car was damaged by a dumpster that was blown around by the wind. Trees were uprooted in Coolidge.
Power poles and lines reported blown down. As many as 70 poles were down in the Buckeye area alone.
Power poles down in central Phoenix.
Large branches blown from trees.
A spotter in Youngtown had a downpour of one inch of rain in just 30 minutes.
Many reports of large hail that accompanied several waves of thunderstorms across the city of Phoenix.
Trees uprooted at 48th street and Mcdowell. Nearby homes damaged.
Numerous trees blown down.
Numerous trees blown down by strong winds.
Trees and power lines down.
Several trees down and a hangar door damaged at the airport.
Microburst winds observed in Mesa near Recker and Brown.

Easterly winds gusted up to 65 knots at Sky Harbor airport. Several aircraft and at least one terminal building was damaged, with debris blown onto the runways and adjacent areas. About 500 people were stranded in the terminals overnight due to flight delays and power outages.

A trained spotter reported a wind gust of 85 mph at 16th St and Thomas. Widespread damage occurred to homes, businesses and windows knocked out in at least one high-rise. Numerous power poles were taken down, and many trees uprooted. Some damage also occurred at the Arizona State Capitol in Phoenix.
Very strong wind gusts reported at Estrella Parkway and Elliott.
In Tempe, an 18 year-old man was injured by a falling tree. Winds on the ASU campus were measured at 69 mph and severely damaged the indoor football practice facility.
Widespread downpours were reported around the Valley with generally one to two inches of rain in a short period. One of the heaviest amounts was 1.89 inches at Gateway Community College in Phoenix.

A fiery multi-vehicle collision pileup occurred on the eastbound lanes of I-10 near Tonopah, AZ. A shallow plume of dense blowing dust was observed on satellite imagery during the time of the accident, and although not officially confirmed, the dust is believed to have played a major role in the cause of the accident. Based on several news articles, twelve vehicles in total, including multiple semi-trucks, passengers vehicles, a van, and a recreational vehicle were involved in the accident. Four confirmed fatalities and eight injuries resulted from the collision pileup.
Video showed near zero visibility along State Route 347 near Riggs Road due to dense blowing dust from strong winds. No accidents nor injuries were reported.
Near zero visibility due to dense blowing dust from strong winds resulted in a minor auto accident near Arizona City. No injuries were reported.

A large mesquite tree was uprooted near the intersection of East Kierland Boulevard and East Greenway Parkway in Scottsdale. The Scottsdale Airport ASOS located less than a mile east of the incident measured a peak wind gust of 44 mph. No injuries were reported.

Heavy rain caused some damage to the Hospice Thrift Store in Yuma.  Several businesses at Southgate Mall reported damage due to standing water. A new daily rainfall record,  0.74 inches,  was set at the Yuma Marine Corps Air Station.

Video footage showed a landspout tornado over an open field near the intersection of Johnson and Yuma Road in Buckeye. Given that this landspout developed over an open field, no damages nor injuries were reported.

Video footage showed visibility dropping down to near zero from a shallow dust channel that crossed Carefree Highway as a result of strong winds. Surface observations at 6:00 PM MST indicated gusts at 30 mph so it was possible that gusts could have been over 40 mph during the moment the video was recorded. No accidents nor injuries were reported.
A mesonet station in the Tonto Basin measured a peak gust of 64 mph.

A medium-sized tree was uprooted in the backyard of a house in Gilbert, with the tree falling on the back of a parked pickup truck. Timing estimated from radar with Mesa Gateway Airport measuring a peak gust of 46 mph at around the same time. No injuries were reported.

Flooding caused the closure of state route 79 after heavy rain moved through the area.  The gage at Magma recorded a storm total of 2.99 inches from the evening of the 10th into the early morning hours on the 11th of July.
Brush fire was started by lightning and grew to about 425 acres. No structures were involved in the fire.

Top wind speeds of 55 to 65 mph were common across many areas. One report was a measured speed of 60 mph at 91st avenue and Jomax. A 58 mph gust was measured at the White Tank mesonet location. A wood fence was damaged and a trailer was overturned in Waddell.
Quartzsite Fire Department reported an estimated gust of 75 mph that blew two tractor trailer trucks off the road.
Large hail was reported across parts of central and western Maricopa County. Most of the reports were for dime to penny size hail.

Somerton police reported power lines down due to very strong winds from thunderstorms. At the peak of the storm, between 2,500 and 3,000 APS customers were without power. A large tree in the 3300 block of 15th Avenue in The Dunes subdivision was knocked down. Power outages were also reported on the Cocopah Reservation at County 18th Street and Avenue D and in the north end of the city of Yuma.
State Route 238 near the intersection with South 99th Avenue in Mobile, AZ was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Intersection of State Route 85 and Maricopa Road in Gila Bend was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from the radar. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Numerous power poles down near 424th and Indian School, or about 2 miles west of Tonopah.
A trained spotter reported a wind gust of 60 mph along with pea sized hail at McClintock and Guadalupe.
Hail to dime size was reported in Wittmann.
About 6 power poles were downed, resulting in power outages for as many as 4500 customers in Queen Creek.

A female hiker hiking the McDowell Sonoran Preserve was found deceased at the trail. A report filed by the Maricopa County Medical Examiner a month later determined the cause of death was due to environmental heat exposure.

Photos taken along Bartlett Dam Rd show evidence of flash flooding over the road in multiple spots, including at the Camp Creek crossing, with many small boulders, sediment, and other debris left over in the road. No injuries were reported.
The intersection of 4th Street and California Avenue in Parker was closed due to flooding. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Video showed Fish Creek Wash experienced flooding, making a low water crossing along Split Mountain Road impassable. Timing estimated from radar. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Heavy rain in Ehrenberg resulted in flooded low spots. Roads were closed between Parker and Poston.

According to Arizona Public Service, 48 power poles across a distance of 3 miles were blown down along Old Highway 80 between Buckeye and Gila Bend. Winds were measured up to 56 mph on the Palo Verde Nuclear Generating Station tower.
Winds were estimated to reach as high as 60 mph along with visibility to less than 1/4 mile in blowing dust.
Flood control district sensor measured a gust to 60 mph.
A RAWS station located along the Belmont Mountain measured a peak wind gust of 85 mph.

Social media photo showed a flooded low water crossing along AZ-72, just northwest of McVay Road, with around 6-12 inches of flowing water over the road. Timing estimated from radar. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Video and photos show 2 to 4 feet of murky floodwater rapidly moving through Pinal Creek, with Beer Tree Crossing impassable. Timing estimated from radar. No damages nor injuries were reported.
A Salt River Project Observing Station located in Coolidge measured a wind gust of 58 mph.

Downed powerlines reported near the intersection of East Randolph Road and North La Palma Road in Coolidge, resulting in a road closure. Timing estimated based on radar. Wind gusts were estimated between 55-60 mph with a reporting site nearby measuring a peak gust of 58 mph. No injuries were reported.
Video showed reduced visibilities of around a quarter mile along 1-10 near Casa Grande due to dense blowing dust from thunderstorm outflow winds. No accident nor injuries were reported.
Live shot from local broadcast station showed visibility dropping to around a quarter mile due to dense blowing dust from thunderstorm outflow winds. No accidents nor injuries were reported.
Broadcast media showed a large house fire from a lightning strike along the area of 121st Avenue and Southern Avenue in Tolleson with the fire causing severe damage. No injuries were reported.

A large mesquite tree was uprooted into the southbound lane of 67th Avenue near the intersection with West Wolf Street in Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated between 55-60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.

Trees were uprooted and a semi trailer was turned over. A peak gust of 57 mph was measured at the Yuma airport. About 1,000 APS customers were left without power due to these thunderstorm winds. Power poles were blown down in the Mohawk area.
The Coolidge police reported dense blowing dust.
Microburst winds hit Chandler airport and flipped at least two planes. Winds also damaged a fence and other property. Northeast winds peaked at 67 mph at 3:25 pm.

Heat was blamed as a factor in 9 deaths in the month of July for Maricopa County. Temperatures in Phoenix were above normal for much of the month, with this month being tied for the 17th warmest on record. The average minimum temperature was the 10th warmest, and a record |warm minimum of 90 degrees was set on July 1st. The high temperature in Phoenix on the 1st was 110.
Large area of blowing dust reported by DPS. At about the same time there was a report of a 52 mph wind at the Yuma Proving Ground.
Winds from a microburst blew down about 25 trees and damaged light poles at Mesa Community College. A security officer was slightly injured when the strong winds blew him from his golf cart.

Around 50 power poles were blown down along a north-south oriented dirt road that passes by the Ormesa 2 Geothermal Site east of Holtville. Timing estimated from radar and winds were estimated at 50-55 mph based on radar and the environment. Damage cost was estimated.

Heavy rain, with rainfall rates of one to 2 inches per hour caused washes to flow. A car was washed away attempting to cross a flooded road near Geronimo and 28th Avenue. A woman and a two year-old were rescued after the car became lodged under a small bridge. Another car was washed away near Val Vista and 16th Avenue. A nearby gage at Delaware and Apache Trail recorded about one inch in 30 minutes up to 641 am.

Thunderstorms moved slowly across southern Gila County during the early morning hours. Considerable runoff led to water in some small streams and creeks. By 730 am, water was reported deep in Pinal Creek with water and small debris flowing rapidly across highway 60 in downtown Globe.
Numerous trees and power lines were downed by strong winds in and near Blythe. Some homes also sustained some damage from these storms.

Video in a parking lot of local shopping area near the area of I-17 and Happy Valley Road in North Phoenix showed large tree branches snapped from a thunderstorm microburst. Wind gusts were estimated upwards of 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Semi-truck overturned on I-17 southbound near Union Hills Drive in North Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated upwards of 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Six inches of flowing water estimated on road near the area of Cave Creek Road and Union Hills Drive in North Phoenix. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Videos sent in showing multiple palo verde trees and branches down near Scottsdale Road and E Princess Drive in Scottsdale. Wind gusts estimated around 50 mph. No injuries were reported.

Few palo verde and tree branches downed in the parking lot of a shopping center located in the area of North Scottsdale Road and Frank Lloyd Wright Boulevard in Scottsdale. Wind gusts were estimated around 50 mph.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Gauge located along East Fork Cave Creek near 7th Avenue showed water levels rising above the alarm stage of 3 feet likely flooding 7th avenue just downstream. Water levels peaked at 3.90 feet at around 12 AM MST before gradually rising below alarm stage at around 1:23 AM MST. No damages or injuries were reported.

Dozens of trees, approximately 50 trees, downed across a section of Surprise generally between Highway U.S. 60 and Bell Road, with a report of a large tree falling through a brick wall and onto a house near the area between Dysart Road and Bell Road. Wind gusts were estimated between 55 and 60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Video shows fast flowing water on the roadway, likely at least 6 inches, in the area of Bell Road and 56th Street in Scottsdale. Timing estimated from radar.

Broadcast showed numerous large tree branches ripped off in a neighborhood located near the area of Bell Road and Tatum Blvd in Scottsdale. A shed ended up on the middle of North 45th Place within the neighborhood as the winds caused the shed to blow over a brick wall and onto the street. Wind gusts were estimated between 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Several roads across the city of Maricopa had standing water from the multiple hours of rain that fell between 12:30 am and 5 am MST. Doppler radar as well as rain gauges measured total rainfall amounts in excess of 2 inches throughout the entire time span. Flooding overall was minor. No damages or injuries were reported.
I-8 near State Route 85 in Gila Bend closed due to all lanes being blocked due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Washes flowing across roadway along State Route 72 southeast of Bouse. No damages or injuries reported.
Images showed power poles toppled near Gold Canyon. Location and timing based on outage map report. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Visibility of less than 1/10 mile reported near Queen Creek due to dense blowing dust from thunderstorm outflow winds. Winds gusts were estimated upwards of 45 mph. No accidents or injuries were reported.
